files.text:
# Wallflower Phenology Data Protocol

A data protocol for recording flowering phenology and petal number of the **Contra Costa wallflower** (*Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum*) on the riverine dunes of **Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge (ADNWR)**, Contra Costa County, California, on the San Joaquin River, together with dune position, river/Delta wind and soil moisture.

The `species` field is retained so other *Erysimum* taxa can still be recorded, but the default taxon and site are now fixed (see below).

## Taxon and site (resolved)

| Item | Default | Notes (verified 2026-11-17) |
|---|---|---|
| Taxon | *Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum* (Contra Costa wallflower) | ITIS TSN 528069. A short-lived perennial or biennial in the mustard family (Brassicaceae). |
| Site | Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge (`site_id` = `ADNWR`) | Riverine (not coastal) sand dunes on the south bank of the San Joaquin River. With few exceptions the taxon is known only from this refuge. |
| Legal status | Federally endangered (listed 1978); California endangered (CE); CNPS Rare Plant Rank 1B.1 | The refuge is closed to the public. It was established in 1980 and also supports the endangered Antioch Dunes evening primrose and Lange's metalmark butterfly. |
| Bloom window | March–August, peak in April (late April in FWS sources) | The CNPS Rare Plant Inventory lists the blooming period as Mar–Jul. Plan fieldwork for March–August, with peak effort in April. |
| Habitat | Open, well-drained, wind-blown sand on riverine dunes, often on north-facing slopes | CNPS: inland dunes, elevations 3–20 m. |
| Pollination | Self-incompatible; bees and possibly hawkmoths | Cross-pollination is required for seed set. Optional pollinator fields are included for that reason. |

Sources for the facts above: the FWS species page, the FWS Antioch Dunes NWR page, EPA interim core-map documentation (2025–2026, quoting the FWS 5-year review), the CNPS Rare Plant Inventory, Calflora, and the Center for Plant Conservation profile. URLs are in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.

## File layout
| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Overview, field steps, permits, open questions |
| `SCHEMA.md` | Field-by-field schema, field renames, USA-NPN phenophase definitions, QA rules |
| `data_dictionary.csv` | Machine-readable schema (47 fields) |
| `wallflower_phenology_template.csv` | Data-entry template (2 rows marked EXAMPLE are fabricated; delete before use) |
| `DATA_SOURCES.md` | Verified public data sources for this taxon and site, how they map to fields, gaps |

## Permits (required before any fieldwork)

The refuge is **closed to the public**. Do not enter, tag plants, or collect data on the refuge without authorization.

1. **USFWS National Wildlife Refuge special use permit (SUP)** from the ADNWR manager, for access and any research activity on the refuge. See [Special Use Permits](https://www.fws.gov/services/permits/special-use-permits).
2. **Federal ESA permit** for any handling of this listed plant (typically a recovery/research permit via [FWS ePermits](https://www.fws.gov/services/permits)).
3. **CDFW authorization** may also be required: the taxon is state-listed as endangered (CE). Check current [CESA](https://wildlife.ca.gov/Conservation/CESA) and [Scientific Collecting](https://wildlife.ca.gov/Licensing/Scientific-Collecting) rules.

**Petal counts must be non-destructive:** count petals on the intact flower, on the plant. Do not pick, clip, or otherwise remove flowers or floral parts.

Until permits are in hand, use only public datasets (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`). Public data cannot supply petal counts, plant-level bloom dates for this variety, dune position, on-dune soil moisture, or plant-height wind.

## Field protocol (short)

0. **Permits first** (above). Do not visit the closed refuge without them.
1. **Setup (once):** Lay out river-normal transects (perpendicular to the San Joaquin River shoreline) from the river shoreline across riverward slope → crest → landward slope → swale → hinterland. Tag plants (`plant_id`). Record lat/lon, elevation + datum, aspect (habitat is often on north-facing, riverward slopes), distance from the river shoreline and from the dune crest, dune zone, and the shoreline datum used.
2. **Each visit** (frequency TBD): For each tagged plant record USA-NPN status 500 Flowers or flower buds and 501 Open flowers (Y/N/?), 501 intensity class, open flower count, and 516 Fruits.
3. **Petals (non-destructive):** On plants with open flowers, count petals on up to 5 fresh flowers still on the plant; record counts and the sample size. No picking.
4. **Pollinators (optional):** Watch a recorded window (minutes) and record taxon group and visit count. Useful because the plant is self-incompatible.
5. **Wind (river/Delta, not coastal):** Read the on-site anemometer at a known height and averaging window, or note the nearest CIMIS, ASOS, or CO-OPS station id and pull the matching hour later. Set `qa_flag=ESTIMATED` for off-site data. See `DATA_SOURCES.md` for the nearest stations.
6. **Soil moisture:** Take a probe VWC at a fixed depth (e.g. 10 cm) next to each plant. Record method and time. Calibrate probes for sand gravimetrically. No nearby SCAN station is close enough to stand in for plant-scale moisture.
7. **Same day:** Enter data, run range checks, set QA flags. Derive bloom dates at season end (see SCHEMA.md).

## Open questions (still undecided)

1. **Species:** resolved — *Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum*.
2. **Site:** resolved — Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge, Contra Costa County, CA.
3. **Time span:** which season(s) and years?
4. **Sampling frequency:** weekly, twice weekly, …? This sets the precision of the derived bloom dates.
5. **Permits vs public data only:** are a refuge SUP and the ESA (and any CDFW) permits obtainable, or should the project rely only on public datasets? Public data cannot fill the gaps listed in `DATA_SOURCES.md`.

# SCHEMA – Contra Costa wallflower (*Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum*) phenology record

One row = one plant (`plant_id`) on one visit. Machine-readable version: `data_dictionary.csv`.

**Defaults:** `species` = `Erysimum capitatum var. angustatum`; `site_id` = `ADNWR` (Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge, Contra Costa County, CA, on the San Joaquin River). The `species` field is still required and is not hard-coded, so other *Erysimum* can be entered if needed.

## Conventions
- **Missing values:** `NA` = not measured / not applicable. For USA-NPN status fields use `?` = observer unsure (USA-NPN convention), never blank.
- **Dates/times:** ISO 8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `HH:MM` 24 h local) plus `timezone` offset (America/Los_Angeles is UTC−08:00 standard / UTC−07:00 PDT).
- **Coordinates:** WGS84 decimal degrees. Elevations need `elevation_datum`.
- **Wind** is river/Delta wind, not coastal wind. Off-site values come from CIMIS, ASOS, or CO-OPS stations listed in `DATA_SOURCES.md`, not from ocean buoys.

## Field renames (from the earlier coastal-dune draft)

Field names that referred to a coastal mean-high-water / foredune frame were renamed for this riverine site. Keep the new names in templates and new data. If you have already collected rows under the old names, map them as follows and record the mapping in `notes`.

| Old name (retired) | New name | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `dist_from_mhw_m` | `dist_from_river_shoreline_m` | Horizontal distance landward of the **San Joaquin River shoreline**, not a coastal MHW line. State the shoreline datum in `shoreline_datum`. A tidal datum at NOAA CO-OPS station 9415064 (Antioch, San Joaquin River) — e.g. MHW or MHHW — is the recommended reference. |
| `dist_from_foredune_crest_m` | `dist_from_dune_crest_m` | Signed distance from the **dune crest** (+landward / −riverward). The coastal "foredune crest" label does not fit these riverine dunes. |
| `dune_zone` allowed values `foredune / swale / backdune / other` | `river_shore / riverward_slope / crest / landward_slope / swale / hinterland / other` | Zones follow a river-normal profile from the San Joaquin River shoreline inland. At ADNWR the river lies to the north, so `riverward_slope` is often the north-facing slope favored by this taxon. |

`wind_source` still accepts `NDBC`, but NDBC ocean buoys are not appropriate here; use `onsite_anemometer`, `CIMIS`, `ASOS`, `CO-OPS`, or `reanalysis`. `CO-OPS` was added as an allowed value for the nearby river meteorological stations.

## Phenology (aligned with USA-NPN / Nature's Notebook)
Verified from the USA-NPN API (`getPhenophasesForSpecies`, species_id 1612 *Erysimum capitatum*; `getPhenophaseDefinitionDetails`). USA-NPN lists the species, not this endangered variety; the phenophase definitions are still the right ones to use in the field.
- **500 Flowers or flower buds** – "One or more fresh open or unopened flowers or flower buds are visible on the plant. Include flower buds that are still developing, but do not include wilted or dried flowers."
- **501 Open flowers** – "One or more open, fresh flowers are visible on the plant. Flowers are considered 'open' when the reproductive parts (male stamens or female pistils) are visible between or within unfolded or open flower parts… Do not include wilted or dried flowers."
- 501 intensity (abundance category 50): "What percentage of all fresh flowers (buds plus unopened plus open) on the plant are open?" – `Less than 5%`, `5-24%`, `25-49%`, `50-74%`, `75-94%`, `95% or more`.
- Other NPN phenophases for *E. capitatum*: 482 Initial growth, 488 Leaves, 516 Fruits, 390 Ripe fruits, 504 Recent fruit or seed drop.

USA-NPN records **status (Y/N/?) per visit**, not event dates. The bloom dates here are **derived** per plant per season:
- `first_bud_date` = first visit with 500 = Y
- `first_flower_date` = first visit with 501 = Y
- `peak_bloom_date` = visit with the highest 501 intensity class (tie-break: highest `open_flower_count`)
- `last_flower_date` = last visit with 501 = Y that is followed by a 501 = N visit
Also keep the preceding N visit date for each: the true event lies between the two (interval-censored).

Expected bloom at this site is March–August, peaking in April (late April in FWS sources). CNPS lists Mar–Jul.

## Petals
Brassicaceae flowers normally have 4 petals. Sample up to `petal_n_flowers_sampled` fresh open flowers per plant (suggested 5, chosen haphazardly across inflorescences). **Counts are non-destructive: count on the plant; do not pick flowers.** Record each count in `petal_counts` (e.g. `4;4;5;4;4`). Set `petal_deviation_flag` = Y if any count ≠ 4.

## Pollinators (optional)
The taxon is self-incompatible, so seed set depends on insect visits. If a watch is done, record `pollinator_taxon_group`, `pollinator_count` (visits or individuals in the window), and `pollinator_obs_window_min`. If more than one group is seen, set the group to `mixed` and list counts by group in `notes`.

## QA flags
`OK`, `SUSPECT` (implausible value, kept), `ESTIMATED` (e.g. wind from off-site station or interpolated), `SENSOR_FAIL`, `REVIEW` (needs a second look). Range checks: VWC 0–60 %, direction 0–360, gust ≥ speed, petal counts 0–10, pollinator counts ≥ 0.

## Field table
| field | type | units | allowed values | required | missing | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `record_id` | string |  | unique | required | — | Unique row id |
| `plant_id` | string |  | unique per plant | required | — | Persistent tag of the individual plant |
| `species` | string |  | binomial or binomial + variety | required | — | Scientific name. Default: Erysimum capitatum var. angustatum |
| `site_id` | string |  | project site list | required | — | Site code. Default: ADNWR |
| `observer` | string |  |  | required | — | Observer initials or id |
| `obs_date` | date | ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD |  | required | — | Local date of visit |
| `obs_time` | time | HH:MM 24h |  | required | NA | Local time of visit |
| `timezone` | string |  | e.g. -07:00 / -08:00 | required | — | UTC offset |
| `npn_500_flowers_or_buds` | categorical |  | Y / N / ? | required | ? | USA-NPN phenophase 500 Flowers or flower buds |
| `npn_501_open_flowers` | categorical |  | Y / N / ? | required | ? | USA-NPN phenophase 501 Open flowers |
| `open_flower_intensity` | categorical |  | <5% / 5-24% / 25-49% / 50-74% / 75-94% / 95% or more | optional | NA | USA-NPN abundance: % of fresh flowers that are open |
| `npn_516_fruits` | categorical |  | Y / N / ? | optional | ? | USA-NPN phenophase 516 Fruits |
| `first_bud_date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD |  | optional (derived) | NA | Derived: first visit with 500=Y (plant-season) |
| `first_flower_date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD |  | optional (derived) | NA | Derived: first visit with 501=Y |
| `peak_bloom_date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD |  | optional (derived) | NA | Derived: visit with max open-flower intensity / open count |
| `last_flower_date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD |  | optional (derived) | NA | Derived: last visit with 501=Y before a 501=N |
| `open_flower_count` | integer | flowers | >=0 | optional | NA | Count of open flowers on plant |
| `petal_n_flowers_sampled` | integer | flowers | 0-10 | required if any petal_counts | NA | Number of open flowers examined for petals (on the plant; non-destructive) |
| `petal_counts` | string | petals | semicolon-separated integers | optional | NA | Petals per sampled flower |
| `petal_deviation_flag` | categorical |  | Y / N | optional | NA | Any sampled flower with petals != 4 |
| `pollinator_taxon_group` | categorical |  | bees / hawkmoths / flies / butterflies / other / mixed / none_observed | optional | NA | Taxon group visiting flowers during the watch |
| `pollinator_count` | integer | visits | >=0 | required if a watch was done | NA | Visit or individual count in the observation window |
| `pollinator_obs_window_min` | decimal | minutes | >0 | required if a watch was done | NA | Length of the pollinator watch |
| `transect_id` | string |  |  | required | — | River-normal dune transect code |
| `dist_from_river_shoreline_m` | decimal | m | >=0 | optional | NA | Horizontal distance landward of the San Joaquin River shoreline (renamed from dist_from_mhw_m) |
| `dist_from_dune_crest_m` | decimal | m |  | optional | NA | Signed distance from dune crest (+landward / −riverward); renamed from dist_from_foredune_crest_m |
| `dune_zone` | categorical |  | river_shore / riverward_slope / crest / landward_slope / swale / hinterland / other | required | — | Position in the riverine dune profile |
| `shoreline_datum` | categorical |  | MHW / MHHW / MLLW / observed_waterline / NAVD88_contour / other | required if dist_from_river_shoreline_m | NA | Datum used to place the river shoreline (recommended: a published datum at CO-OPS 9415064) |
| `elevation_m` | decimal | m (state datum e.g. NAVD88) |  | optional | NA | Ground elevation |
| `elevation_datum` | string |  | NAVD88 / other | required if elevation_m | NA | Vertical datum |
| `lat` | decimal | degrees | -90..90 | required | — | Latitude WGS84 |
| `lon` | decimal | degrees | -180..180 | required | — | Longitude WGS84 |
| `gps_accuracy_m` | decimal | m | >=0 | optional | NA | GPS horizontal accuracy |
| `aspect_deg` | decimal | degrees true | 0-360 or FLAT | optional | NA | Slope aspect (direction slope faces) |
| `wind_speed_ms` | decimal | m/s | >=0 | optional | NA | Mean river/Delta wind speed |
| `wind_gust_ms` | decimal | m/s | >=0 | optional | NA | Peak gust |
| `wind_dir_deg` | decimal | degrees true | 0-360 | optional | NA | Direction wind is FROM |
| `wind_source` | categorical |  | onsite_anemometer / CIMIS / ASOS / CO-OPS / NDBC / reanalysis | required if wind_speed_ms | NA | Source of wind data (use river/Delta stations, not ocean buoys) |
| `wind_station_id` | string |  | e.g. CIMIS 247 / KCCR / 9415115 | optional | NA | Station id if not on-site |
| `wind_avg_window_min` | decimal | minutes | e.g. 2 / 10 / 60 | required if wind_speed_ms | NA | Averaging window for mean speed |
| `wind_sensor_height_m` | decimal | m | >0 | required if wind_speed_ms | NA | Sensor height above ground (or above the station's stated reference) |
| `soil_vwc_pct` | decimal | % (m3/m3 x100) | 0-60 | optional | NA | Volumetric water content |
| `soil_depth_cm` | decimal | cm | >0 | required if soil_vwc_pct | NA | Measurement depth |
| `soil_method` | categorical |  | probe_TDR / probe_FDR / gravimetric | required if soil_vwc_pct | NA | Soil moisture method |
| `soil_time` | time | HH:MM |  | required if soil_vwc_pct | NA | Local time of soil measurement |
| `qa_flag` | categorical |  | OK / SUSPECT / ESTIMATED / SENSOR_FAIL / REVIEW | required | — | Quality flag |
| `notes` | string |  |  | optional | — | Free text; EXAMPLE rows must say EXAMPLE |

# Public data sources (checked 2026-11-17)

Each URL below returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-17, fetched with curl or WebFetch (GET used when HEAD was blocked or returned 405). License notes are summaries; check each provider's current terms before publishing. Distances are great-circle kilometres from NOAA CO-OPS station 9415064 (Antioch, San Joaquin River; 38.02, −121.815), which is the published river station next to the refuge, not a surveyed refuge centroid.

This revision is for *Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum* at Antioch Dunes National Wildlife Refuge (riverine dunes). Coastal products from the earlier draft that do not apply here are listed at the end and were not reused as wind or shoreline sources.

## Taxon and site references
| Source | What it confirms | URL | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| FWS species page | Contra Costa wallflower; *Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum*; short-lived perennial; almost only at ADNWR; riverbank dunes on the San Joaquin River | https://www.fws.gov/species/contra-costa-wallflower-erysimum-capitatum-var-angustatum | 200 |
| FWS Antioch Dunes NWR | Refuge established 1980 to protect this wallflower, the Antioch Dunes evening primrose, and Lange's metalmark butterfly; historically a riverine sand-dune ecosystem; **closed to the public** | https://www.fws.gov/refuge/antioch-dunes | 200 |
| EPA interim core-map documentation | Endangered biennial/short-lived perennial; blooms March–August, peak in April; open, sandy, well-drained soils; wind-blown sand, often north-facing slopes; self-incompatible; bees and possibly hawkmoths; listed as endangered in 1978 | https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2026-01/contra-costa-wallflower-documentation.pdf | 200 |
| FWS 5-year review (PDF, cited by EPA) | Date listed given as 26 April 1978, 43 FR 17910; peak bloom late April; self-incompatible; bees and possibly hawkmoths | https://ecos.fws.gov/docs/tess/species_nonpublish/993.pdf | 200 |
| FWS ECOS profile | Listed endangered; ECOS "date listed" 27 May 1978 | https://ecos.fws.gov/ecp/species/7601 | 200 |
| CNPS Rare Plant Inventory (v9.6.16) | CRPR 1B.1; FE; CE; G5T1 / S1; perennial herb; inland dunes, 3–20 m; blooming period Mar–Jul; known only from the Antioch Dunes; 5 CNDDB element occurrences | https://rareplants.cnps.org/Plants/Details?taxon=Erysimum%20capitatum%20var.%20angustatum | 200 (GET; HEAD returned 405) |
| Calflora taxon page (crn 9942) | Federal endangered, California endangered, CRPR 1B.1; **~18 records** | https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=9942 | 200 |
| Center for Plant Conservation (CPC 1828) | Duration biennial or perennial; endemic to the Antioch Dunes, Contra Costa County | https://saveplants.org/plant-profile/?CPCNum=1828 | 200 |
| ITIS | TSN 528069, *Erysimum capitatum* var. *angustatum* | https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=528069 | 200 |

The FWS 5-year review and the ECOS profile use different calendar dates in 1978 for "date listed" (26 April vs 27 May). This protocol states only that the taxon was federally listed as endangered in 1978.

## Permits
| Source | Use | URL | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| FWS Special Use Permits | Refuge SUP for access or research on a National Wildlife Refuge | https://www.fws.gov/services/permits/special-use-permits | 200 |
| FWS ePermits | Federal ESA recovery/research and other FWS permits | https://www.fws.gov/services/permits | 200 |
| CDFW CESA | California Endangered Species Act context (taxon is CE) | https://wildlife.ca.gov/Conservation/CESA | 200 |
| CDFW Scientific Collecting | Starting point for CDFW scientific collecting rules | https://wildlife.ca.gov/Licensing/Scientific-Collecting | 200 |

## Phenology / occurrence
| Source | Variables | Resolution | Access | URL | License / terms | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| USA-NPN / Nature's Notebook | Phenophase status Y/N/? (500, 501, 516…), intensity | Per plant per visit | REST API (`services.usanpn.org/npn_portal/...`), data download | https://www.usanpn.org/data/observational ; https://services.usanpn.org/npn_portal/phenophases/getPhenophases.json | USA-NPN data use policy (attribution) | `npn_*`, `open_flower_intensity`, derived bloom dates. **Species-level *E. capitatum* only — the variety is not in the NPN list.** |
| GBIF | Occurrence records (date, coordinates, sometimes `reproductiveCondition`) | Point records | REST API `api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search` | https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match?name=Erysimum%20capitatum%20var.%20angustatum | Per record: CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-NC | `species`, `obs_date`, `lat`/`lon` |
| iNaturalist (API) | Observations + "Flowers and Fruits" annotation (term 12: 13 Flowers, 14 Fruits or Seeds, 15 Flower Buds) | Point records, photo-based | API `api.inaturalist.org/v1/observations` | https://api.inaturalist.org/v1/taxa?q=Contra%20Costa%20wallflower (taxon_id **119564**) | Per observation CC license (observer chosen) | `npn_500`/`npn_501` (approximately), `obs_date`, `lat`/`lon`. Many public coordinates for this listed plant are likely masked. |
| Calflora | CA plant occurrence records | Point records | Web search/download | https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=9942 | Calflora terms of use | `species`, `lat`/`lon` |
| CNPS Rare Plant Inventory | Rare plant rank, listed status, habitat, published blooming period | Species-level; 5 CNDDB EOs | Web | https://rareplants.cnps.org/Plants/Details?taxon=Erysimum%20capitatum%20var.%20angustatum ; https://rareplants.cnps.org/ | CNPS terms | `species` context only (not per-plant visit data) |

### Counts for this variety (queried 2026-11-17)
- **iNaturalist API:** taxon_id 119564 (*Erysimum capitatum angustatum*, Contra Costa wallflower) — **57** observations, of which **49** research grade; annotations: **13** Flowers, **2** Flower Buds, **4** Fruits or Seeds. These are presence-only records on the date seen, not first/peak/last bloom dates. EPA (document dated October 2025) reported 54 research-grade observations at that time.
[line omitted from the public board]
- **Calflora:** the taxon page itself states **~18 records**.
- **CNPS / CNDDB:** **5** element occurrences (not individual plants).
[line omitted from the public board]
- **Petal counts:** no public per-flower petal-count dataset for this taxon was found on these platforms.

## River shoreline, water level, and elevation
| Source | Variables | Resolution | Access | URL | License | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
[line omitted from the public board]
[line omitted from the public board]
| USGS 3DEP via The National Map Downloader | Inland topographic DEMs / lidar where available | Survey-dependent | Web downloader | https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/ | USGS, public domain | `elevation_m`, `aspect_deg`, `dist_from_dune_crest_m` (crest derived from a DEM) |

## Wind / weather (river and Delta, not coastal)
| Source | Variables | Resolution | Access | URL | License | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CIMIS (California DWR) | Wind speed/direction, ET, temperature; station list in the official i04 dataset | Hourly/daily; CA stations | Web, API (key); station list CSV | https://cimis.water.ca.gov/ ; https://cimis.water.ca.gov/Stations.aspx ; https://data.ca.gov/@california-department-of-water-resources/i04-cimis-weather-stations ; CSV: https://gis.data.cnra.ca.gov/api/download/v1/items/1e3309caa3fe460faef12e8dc5afc85f/csv?layers=0 | CA DWR terms | `wind_*` (`wind_source=CIMIS`) |
| UC IPM station lists (cross-check) | Confirms CIMIS #47 Brentwood (1985–present) and #170 Concord (2001–present), plus the nearby NCDC/COOP "Antioch Pumping Plant 3" | Station list | Web | https://ipm.ucanr.edu/WEATHER/wxallstnames.html ; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/WEATHER/SITES/contracosta.html | UC IPM | station identification |
| Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS | ASOS/AWOS METAR wind, gust, direction | Hourly METAR, some 1-min | Web/CGI download | https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/download.phtml?network=CA_ASOS ; KCCR: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/sites/site.php?network=CA_ASOS&station=CCR ; KSCK: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/sites/site.php?network=CA_ASOS&station=SCK | Free; IEM acknowledgement requested | `wind_*`, `wind_source=ASOS` |
[line omitted from the public board]
| NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database | Station hourly wind, weather (includes ASOS) | Hourly/sub-hourly | Download, API | https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/integrated-surface-database | US Gov | `wind_*` |
| ERA5 (Copernicus CDS) | 10 m u/v wind, gusts, soil water layers | Hourly, 0.25° | CDS API (account) | https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels | Copernicus licence (attribution) | `wind_*` (`reanalysis`), gridded soil moisture context |
| Open-Meteo Historical API | Reanalysis wind and soil moisture by lat/lon | Hourly | No-key REST API | https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api | Data CC BY 4.0 (attribution) | `wind_*` (`reanalysis`) |

### Nearest stations to the Antioch river station (9415064)

**CIMIS** (coordinates and Active status from the DWR i04 CIMIS Weather Stations dataset, accessed 2026-11-17; the dataset's `Date_Data_Refers_To` is 2023-02-08):
- **#247 Jersey Island** (Contra Costa) — 38.033386, −121.701247; about **10 km**; Active; connected 2016-07-01. Closest CIMIS station.
- **#140 Twitchell Island** (Sacramento County, across the river) — 38.121739, −121.674455; about **17 km**; Active; connected 1997-10-08.
- **#47 Brentwood** (Contra Costa) — 37.928154, −121.65973; about **17 km**; Active; connected 1985-11-18.
- **#170 Concord** (Contra Costa) — 38.015372, −122.020278; about **18 km**; Active; connected 2001-04-06.

**ASOS** (IEM CA_ASOS metadata, 2026-11-17):
- **KCCR / CCR** Concord/Buchanan Field — 37.99161, −122.05263; about **21 km** west; archive begins 1969-01-01. Nearest ASOS.
- **C83** Byron — about 27 km; **KSUU** Travis AFB — about 29 km.
- **KSCK / SCK** Stockton Metro — 37.89417, −121.23831; about **53 km** east. Farther than KCCR; listed because it is a long-record Central Valley station.

**CO-OPS wind (sensors confirmed "Wind", status 1):**
- **9415115 Pittsburg, Suisun Bay** — 38.041557, −121.886665; about **7 km**; wind sensor elevation 25.0 ft above site elevation (about 7.6 m). Closest official river wind sensor. Established 2011-03-08.
- **9415144 Port Chicago** — about **20 km**; wind sensor elevation 27.70 ft above site elevation (about 8.4 m), plus observed water levels.

Off-site wind is always `qa_flag=ESTIMATED`. It is exposed-station or river-channel wind, not plant-height wind on the dune.

## Soil moisture
| Source | Variables | Resolution | Access | URL | License | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NASA SMAP | Surface (~top 5 cm) soil moisture | Coarse grid (L3 SPL3SMP ~36 km), daily | NSIDC DAAC (Earthdata login) | https://smap.jpl.nasa.gov/ ; https://nsidc.org/data/spl3smp (redirects to the current version page) | NASA open data | Regional context only for `soil_vwc_pct` |
| USDA NRCS SCAN | Soil moisture/temperature at multiple depths, plus wind | Hourly, station network | NWCC web/report generator | https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/resources/data-and-reports/soil-climate-analysis-network ; station list: https://wcc.sc.egov.usda.gov/nwcc/yearcount?counttype=statelist&network=scan | USDA, public domain | **Not usable as a local proxy here.** Nearest SCAN station in the IEM SCAN inventory is Monocline Ridge (S2217), about **198 km** away. |
| ERA5 / Open-Meteo | Gridded soil-water layers | Coarse grid, hourly | See wind table | (same URLs as above) | See above | Regional context only |

CIMIS stations in this area report weather and evapotranspiration. This turn did not verify a volumetric soil-moisture sensor at Jersey Island, Twitchell Island, Brentwood, or Concord, so they are not listed as soil-moisture sources.

## Does public bloom or petal data exist for this variety?
Public portals have only opportunistic occurrence records (see counts above). They can show that a plant was flowering on the day it was photographed or collected. They do not provide first, peak, or last bloom dates for tagged plants, petal counts, dune position, on-dune soil moisture, or plant-height wind. EPA, citing FWS, also noted 726 documented occurrences within ADNWR in FWS recovery-plan material — those are agency records, not a public visit-level phenology table.

## Gaps (not publicly available; require permitted fieldwork)
- Petal counts per flower, and any petal data resolved by dune position.
- Plant-level first bud, first flower, peak and last flower dates for *E. capitatum* var. *angustatum*.
- Dune position (transect, distance from the river shoreline or crest, zone) attached to plant records. It can be estimated from a DEM and GPS after authorized mapping, but it is not published with public occurrences.
- On-dune soil moisture at plant scale. SMAP and reanalysis are far too coarse; no SCAN station is near the refuge.
- Wind at plant height on the dune. CIMIS, ASOS, and CO-OPS give nearby exposed or river-channel wind, not microsite wind.
- Pollinator visits to tagged plants.

## Coastal products not used for this site
These URLs still returned 200, but they are coastal (open-coast shoreline, waves, or ocean buoys) and are not the right references for riverine dunes on the San Joaquin River:
- NOAA Digital Coast / Data Access Viewer: https://coast.noaa.gov/dataviewer/ ; https://coast.noaa.gov/digitalcoast/
- USGS Coastal Change Hazards Portal: https://marine.usgs.gov/coastalchangehazardsportal/
- CDIP (Scripps) wave buoys: https://cdip.ucsd.edu/
- NDBC ocean buoys: https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov/

Use CO-OPS 9415064 datums and USGS 3DEP instead of a coastal MHW / foredune frame. `wind_source=NDBC` remains in the schema only for compatibility; do not use an ocean buoy as the wind source for ADNWR.

## URLs dropped or replaced (failed the 2026-11-17 check, or redirected to the wrong page)
- https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/119564-Erysimum-capitatum-angustatum and https://www.inaturalist.org/pages/annotations: 403 (site blocks this fetcher). Replaced by the iNaturalist API URLs, which returned 200.
- http://www.cimis.water.ca.gov/stations.aspx: HTTP 500. Replaced by https://cimis.water.ca.gov/Stations.aspx.
- https://ipm.ucanr.edu/calludt.cgi/WXDESCRIPTION?STN=BRNTWOOD.A and the Concord equivalent: 404. Station identification uses the IPM lists and the official DWR i04 dataset instead.
- https://ipm.ucanr.edu/WEATHER/wxstndata.html and https://ipm.ucanr.edu/WEATHER/wxstnfo.html: 404.
- https://www.fws.gov/special-use-permits: redirected to a different refuge (Red Rock Lakes). Use https://www.fws.gov/services/permits/special-use-permits.
- https://www.fws.gov/service/3-200-55-endangered-and-threatened-species-recovery-permits and https://www.fws.gov/service/3-200-200-endangered-species-recovery-permits: 404. Use https://www.fws.gov/services/permits (ePermits).
- https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program and https://www.usgs.gov/the-national-map-data-delivery: 403 from this fetcher. Elevation access is given as https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/ (200).
- https://rareplants.cnps.org/Plants/TaxonReport/796: 404. The working inventory URL is https://rareplants.cnps.org/Plants/Details?taxon=Erysimum%20capitatum%20var.%20angustatum (200 on GET; HEAD returned 405).
- CNPS official inventory home https://rareplants.cnps.org/ : 200 on GET; HEAD returned 405.

Older failures from the 2026-10-25 coastal draft (kept only as history): https://www.usanpn.org/data/npn_api (404); several USGS coastal program pages (403/404); https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/programs-initiatives/scan (404; the /resources SCAN page still works).
